history.summary: Ancient Devi shrine on the banks of the Baner (Ban Ganga) River at Chamunda, ~10 km west of Palampur, considered one of the 51 Shakti Peethas and the abode of Shiva and Shakti (hence 'Chamunda Nandikeshwar Dham'). Legend says ~400 years ago a local king and a Brahmin priest received the goddess's permission in a dream to shift her idol from an inaccessible hill site to the present location. The temple complex includes a cave shrine of Shiva (Nandikeshwar), images of Bhairav and Hanuman flanking the main sanctum as guardians, and a large pond; a cremation ground serving 22 nearby villages lies close by. Exact founding date is CONFLICTING across sources (verify); the temple is administered by the Himachal Pradesh government.

name: Chamunda Devi Temple
town_description: Chamunda is a small temple town in Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh, on the banks of the Baner River at the foot of the Dhauladhar range. It exists around the famous Chamunda Devi shrine and draws pilgrims year-round, especially during Navratri. The nearest market towns are Palampur (~10 km east) and Dharamshala (~15 km north). CSV town 'Palampur' corrected: the temple is at Chamunda, not in Palampur itself.

travel.road: On the Palampur-Dharamshala road (NH-154 corridor); regular buses and taxis from Palampur (~10 km) and Dharamshala (~15 km)

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November; Navratri is the peak pilgrimage period
